The test image shows a tomato field with widespread whole-plant wilting — plants are collapsed/drooping across many rows. This is a whole-plant wilt symptom pattern.

Key features: complete plant collapse, field-wide distribution, plants prostrate on soil, still green but severely wilted.

Top candidates: Bacterial_Wilt, Southern_Bacterial_Wilt, Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato.

Now I'll view one reference image from Bacterial_Wilt (whole_plant).

The reference Bacterial_Wilt image shows wilting/drooping plants with brown desiccated tissue — consistent with vascular wilt. 

The test image shows a more dramatic field-wide collapse with plants completely prostrate, still mostly green (sudden collapse). This pattern — field-scale rapid complete wilt of otherwise green plants — is highly characteristic of Bacterial_Wilt (Ralstonia solanacearum), which causes sudden complete wilting across a field via vascular colonization.
